warnings.title: Minor Flood Warning for Warrill Creek
warnings.issued: Issued at 11:52 am AEST on Saturday 28 November 2026
warnings.text:
IDQ20809
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology

Minor Flood Warning for Warrill Creek

Issued at 11:52 am AEST on Saturday 28 November 2026
Flood Warning Number: 3


MINOR FLOODING OCCURRING AT AMBERLEY

Moderate to locally heavy rainfall across the Warrill Creek catchment during Friday has
caused river and creek level rises. A moderate flood peak was observed at Harrisville
early Saturday morning with the river level falling below the minor flood level late
Saturday morning. Minor flooding is occurring downstream at Amberley, where a minor flood
peak is possible Saturday afternoon.

Further showers and storms are forecast across the catchment for the remainder of the
weekend, which may cause further river level rises. The situation is being closely
monitored and warnings will be updated as required.
A Flood Watch is current for parts of southern and southeast Queensland.

Warrill Creek:
Minor flooding is occurring along Warrill Creek.

The Warrill Creek at Harrisville peaked at 4.04 m around 6:00 am Saturday, with moderate
flooding. The Warrill Creek at Harrisville is currently at 2.75 m and falling, below the
minor flood level. The Warrill Creek at Harrisville may remain below the minor flood level
(3.00 m) during Saturday. Renewed rises are possible with forecast rain.

The Warrill Creek at Amberley is currently at 4.34 m and rising, with minor flooding. The
Warrill Creek at Amberley may reach around 4.60 m Saturday afternoon, with minor flooding.
Further rises are possible as upstream flows arrive.

Safety Advice:
* Don't drive, walk, swim or play in floodwater because it is dangerous.
* Stay away from flooded drains, rivers, streams and waterways.
* Obey road closure signs. Plan ahead so you don't drive on flooded roads.
* Check the ABC and local media for updates. The situation can change quickly, so stay
informed.
* For local emergency management warnings and advice visit
www.disaster.qld.gov.au/warnings.

For emergency assistance call SES on telephone number 132 500. In life-threatening
emergencies, call 000 (triple zero) immediately.

Next issue:
The next warning will be issued by 12:00 PM AEST on Sunday 29 November 2026.

warnings.title: Flood Warning for Teviot Brook
warnings.issued: Issued at 9:29 am AEST on Saturday 28 November 2026
warnings.text:
IDQ20815
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology

Flood Warning for Teviot Brook

Issued at 9:29 am AEST on Saturday 28 November 2026
Flood Warning Number: 2


MODERATE FLOODING OCCURRING ALONG TEVIOT BROOK

Moderate to locally heavy rainfall across the Logan-Albert catchment during Friday has
caused rapid river and creek level rises, with the heaviest falls observed across the
Teviot Brook catchment. Minor to major flooding occurred along Teviot Brook overnight
Friday into Saturday. Moderate flooding is continuing but easing as river levels fall.

Further showers and storms are forecast across the catchments for the remainder of the
weekend, which may cause renewed river and creek level rises. The situation is being
closely monitored and warnings will be updated as required.
A Flood Watch is current for parts of southern and southeast Queensland, including the
Logan-Albert and Teviot Brook catchments.

Logan River to Yarrahappini:
Moderate flooding is easing along the Teviot Brook at Harpers Crossing, Boonah, and
Coulson Crossing.

warnings.text:
IDQ20900
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology
This Flood Watch provides early advice of possible flooding within the
specified catchments

Flood Watch for parts of Southern and South East Queensland

Issued at 11:23 am AEST on Saturday 28 November 2026
Flood Watch Number: 2

FLOOD WARNINGS ARE CURRENT, WITH FURTHER MINOR FLOODING POSSIBLE ACROSS THE
FLOOD WATCH AREA OVER THE WEEKEND

A trough with areas of rain and embedded thunderstorms will continue to move
across Queensland from the west over the weekend. Moderate to locally heavy
rainfall with storms is forecast across the southern interior during Saturday
and about the south-east during Sunday, before clearing offshore by Monday.
Catchments are moderately wet to wet in south-east Queensland, and dry to
moderate through most of the southern interior. Catchments may respond quickly
to rainfall, especially in the south-east.
Further river level rises, localised flooding, and minor riverine flooding are
possible across the Flood Watch area over the weekend and into next week.
Significant uncertainty remains in the location and timing of the heaviest
falls. Higher river and creek levels may be possible in some areas.

Catchments likely to be affected include:

   Lower Brisbane River          (for Bremer River and Lockyer and Laidley
   Creeks. Not including Lower Brisbane River itself)

   Logan and Albert Rivers

   Macintyre River               (including Macintyre Brook and Dumaresq
   River)

   Weir River

   Moonie River

   Condamine Rivers

   Balonne River                 (including Maranoa River and Bungil Creek)

   The Big Warrambool River

   Wallam and Mungallala Creeks

   Warrego River (QLD)

Flood warnings are current for the following catchment(s) : Warrill Creek.
Teviot Brook, Paroo, Diamantina, Barcoo, Cooper and Bulloo

warnings.title: IDQ21035
warnings.text:
IDQ21035
Australian Government Bureau of Meteorology

TOP PRIORITY FOR IMMEDIATE BROADCAST

Severe Thunderstorm Warning - Southeast Queensland
For people in Scenic Rim, Southern Downs, Toowoomba and Lockyer Valley Council Areas.

Issued at 2:27 am Sunday, 29 November 2026.

Isolated thunderstorms with moderate rainfall continue, but heavy falls have temporarily eased.

Severe thunderstorms in the warning area have temporarily eased. However, the redevelopment of severe thunderstorms remains possible. The situation is being closely monitored and further detailed warnings will be issued as necessary.

69.6 mm was recorded at Inglewood Bridge in the 2 hours to 12:30 am.

Emergency services advise people to:
    * Stay out of flood water. Never drive, walk, play or ride through it. It is dangerous. 
    * Stay away from storm water drains. 
    * Stay away from fallen powerlines. 
    * Drive slowly. If the road is flooded or damaged, turn around and go another way. 
    * For storm help, call the SES on 132 500 or use the free SES Assistance QLD app. 
 

The next warning is due to be issued by 3:30 am.

A more general severe thunderstorm warning is also current for parts of the Central Highlands and Coalfields, Wide Bay and Burnett, Darling Downs and Granite Belt and Southeast Coast districts. Other warnings may be current.

Check https://www.bom.gov.au/weather-and-climate/warnings-and-alerts. Warnings are also available through TV and Radio broadcasts or call 1300 659 210. The Bureau and emergency services would appreciate warnings being broadcast regularly.
